problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14043558/assets/7f997f7647886e1eea24d292ddd66b2d331d6f7d4c7ffe47b6a52b52dd029a44.png)

Consider the RL circuit shown above. Given that the current $I(t)$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
I(t)=A{e}^{-6t}+\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),
$$

where $A,$ $\alpha ,$ and $\beta $ are constants, find the value of $\alpha +\beta .$
worked_solution:
The diagram shows a series RL circuit with a source electromotive force (EMF) of $4\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\,\text{V},$ a resistor of resistance $12\,Ω,$ and an inductor of inductance $2\,\text{H}.$

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RL circuit, there are two voltage drops:

- The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality $R=12\,Ω.$

$$
{V}_{R}=12I
$$

- The voltage drop across the inductor is proportional to the rate of change of current, with a constant of proportionality $L=2\,\text{H}.$

$$
{V}_{L}=2\cdot \frac{dI}{dt}
$$

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, the differential equation governing the amount of current $I$ in the circuit is

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)=12I+2\cdot \frac{dI}{dt}
$$

which gives the equation

$$
\frac{dI}{dt}+6I=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).
$$

This is a first-order linear equation with constant coefficients. So, to find the general solution, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

- To find the complementary solution ${I}_{c},$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
\frac{d{I}_{c}}{dt}+6{I}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving using an integration technique, such as separation of variables, we obtain the complementary solution

$$
{I}_{c}(t)=A{e}^{-6t},
$$

where $A$ is a constant of integration.

- Next, we find the particular solution. Note that the right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is sinusoidal with argument $3t.$ So, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal with argument $3t,$ i.e.,

$$
{I}_{p}(t)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{p} & =\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t), \\ \frac{d{I}_{p}}{dt} & =-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t),\end{aligned}
$$

into the inhomogeneous equation and group like terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))+6(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ (-3\alpha +6\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+(6\alpha +3\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3\alpha +6\beta =2\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) \\ 6\alpha +3\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{2}{15},$ $\beta =\frac{4}{15}.$ Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{I}_{p}(t)=-\frac{2}{15}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\frac{4}{15}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).
$$

Now, since the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution, the general solution in our case is

$$
I(t)={I}_{c}(t)+{I}_{p}(t)=A{e}^{-6t}-\frac{2}{15}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\frac{4}{15}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\alpha =-\frac{2}{15},\,\beta =\frac{4}{15}
$$

which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha +\beta  & =-\frac{2}{15}+\frac{4}{15} \\  & =\frac{2}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the RL circuit shown above. Given that the current I(t) at time t seconds is given by I(t)=Ae−6t+αcos⁡(3t)+βsin⁡(3t), where A, α, and β are constants, find the value of α+β.

a
815
b
215
c
415

115

Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram shows a series RL circuit with a source electromotive force (EMF) of 4sin⁡(3t)V, a resistor of resistance 12Ω, and an inductor of inductance 2H.

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RL circuit, there are two voltage drops:

  • The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality R=12Ω. VR=12I

  • The voltage drop across the inductor is proportional to the rate of change of current, with a constant of proportionality L=2H. VL=2⋅dIdt

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, the differential equation governing the amount of current I in the circuit is

4sin⁡(3t)=12I+2⋅dIdt

which gives the equation dIdt+6I=2sin⁡(3t).

This is a first-order linear equation with constant coefficients. So, to find the general solution, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

  • To find the complementary solution Ic, we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by dIcdt+6Ic=0. Solving using an integration technique, such as separation of variables, we obtain the complementary solution Ic(t)=Ae−6t, where A is a constant of integration.

  • Next, we find the particular solution. Note that the right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is sinusoidal with argument 3t. So, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal with argument 3t, i.e., Ip(t)=αcos⁡(3t)+βsin⁡(3t). To find the values of α and β, we substitute Ip=αcos⁡(3t)+βsin⁡(3t),dIpdt=−3αsin⁡(3t)+3βcos⁡(3t), into the inhomogeneous equation and group like terms on the left-hand side: (−3αsin⁡(3t)+3βcos⁡(3t))+6(αcos⁡(3t)+βsin⁡(3t))=2sin⁡(3t)(−3α+6β)sin⁡(3t)+(6α+3β)cos⁡(3t)=2sin⁡(3t) Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations: {−3α+6β=2(equating the coefficients ofsin⁡(3t))6α+3β=0(equating the coefficients ofcos⁡(3t)) Solving this system gives α=−215, β=415. Therefore, the particular solution is Ip(t)=−215cos⁡(3t)+415sin⁡(3t).

Now, since the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution, the general solution in our case is I(t)=Ic(t)+Ip(t)=Ae−6t−215cos⁡(3t)+415sin⁡(3t).

Therefore, we have α=−215,β=415 which gives α+β=−215+415=215.
